correctness.rationale: With U=Σu_i, V=Σv_j, hat integration gives diagonal blocks diag(u_i V/3), diag(v_j U/3) and cross block u vᵀ/6. Block multiplication verifies the inverse: diagonal terms 3/(u_i V) or 3/(v_j U), a same-shore all-ones correction 1/(UV), and cross entries −2/(UV). For U_k of weight w=u_k/U, the dimensionless kernel endpoints (multiply by UV) are (1+3/w,−2) on incident edges and (1,−2) on other edges. Absolute affine integration gives ((3+w)²+4w²)/(6(1+w))+5(1−w)/6=g(w). Interpolation of endpoint kernels strictly lowers the evaluation norm below the larger endpoint bound at interior points because the endpoint kernels have opposite signs on a positive-length segment. Sign inputs attain the vertex evaluation norms, which give the essential supremum by continuity. Symmetry gives the L¹ norm by duality. As g decreases strictly, the optimum for fixed a,b comes from maximizing the smallest factor to 1/max(a,b), with the frozen statement's exact condition on both shores, not necessarily uniformity on the smaller shore. Small positive factors approach the unattained supremum 7/3. Since P1=1 the negative part of each row integrates to (g(w)−1)/2. Three independent rational configurations agree exactly with the matrix and row-integral identities.
residual_risks: Rational checks are bounded tests; the matrix and kernel identities establish the assertion for arbitrary positive real factors.

evidence: In the broader atom-free deficit, the edge term is ℓ_ij a_ki a_kj/(a_ki+a_kj) for inverse entry magnitudes a. In units 1/(UV) these endpoint magnitudes are 1+3/w or 1, and 2. Their incident and nonincident masses are wUV and (1−w)UV.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The deficit is 2w(w+3)/(3(w+1))+2(1−w)/3=2/3+4w/[3(1+w)], giving g(w) and the same norming points and sign inputs. Monotonicity and the two simplex constraints give exactly the fixed-size optimization, and P1=1 gives the negative excursion. This is a specialization of the general rule and independently a weighted row-copy application of the star result.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For a U-vertex, set ℓ_i=u_i V and S=UV in the leaf kernel, reversing the edge coordinate to start at the leaf. Its endpoint values are exactly those of the graph's U-row on every U_iV_j, independent of j; summed edge lengths are ℓ_i. This identity also holds on the other shore with ℓ_j=v_j U. One can verify the copying without inverting the new mass matrix: put the star inverse leaf coefficients on the U-vertices and its center coefficient identically on all V-vertices. In the reproducing equations, tests at U_i aggregate to the star leaf equation; each V_j equation is v_j/V times the star center equation, with right side zero. This works for two leaves as well by the same row identity. The exact vertex law is the star law twice, not merely a similar scalar formula.

value.rationale: Sharp stability and positivity defects of graph splines are useful, but in this family the vertex norms reduce directly to the known star leaf rows and the global extrema are consequences of the simplex constraints. The frozen record does not establish an independently useful exact invariant beyond this reduction.
residual_risks: This verdict does not assess other length matrices, higher degrees or a genuinely broader weighted cloning theorem.
